    Zigzag walks (for Fischbacher's Lemma 5.2) #

    A zigzag walk from b back to b (Fischbacher, Lemma 5.2) descends a path v' to a peak d₀, then runs through segments dᵢ ⇜ cᵢ₊₁ ⇝ dᵢ₊₁ (a t-path and an s-path out of the valley cᵢ₊₁), and climbs a path w' from the last peak back to b. Segments are kept as a list (ZWalk.segs) so that §5.3 can insert new peaks by list surgery. This file sets up the walks, their vertex sets and convex hulls (ZWalk.hull).

                        structure LargeIndecomposable.RayCat.ZWalk.Good {A : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} A] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms A] {b : A} (z : ZWalk b) [IsRayCategory A] {a : A} (w : Quiver.Path (RayVert.mk a) (RayVert.mk b)) :
                        Prop

                        The conditions of Fischbacher's proof of Lemma 5.2 for a walk relative to a path w : a ⇝ b: (0) w runs through the last peak and ends with w'; (1) the s-paths are nonzero; the pieces are nontrivial; (2) every inner peak is separating in the hull; (3) consecutive peaks are incomparable.
